To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the strength of monsoonal intraseasonal modes have been decreasing during the past six decade, and this is associated with a redistribution of rainfall intensity from low-frequency modes to non-periodic extreme events.

the intensity of low-frequency intraseaonal oscillations (ISO) over India has decreased over the past 6 decades, which is compensated by a rise in the occurrence and intensity of extreme rainfall events.
the relative strength in the northward-propagation of low-frequency ISO modes of Indian summer Monsoon has been decreasing during the past six-decade.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the changing nature of monsoon ISO and associated extreme rainfall events over India.
understanding the changing nature of rainfall variability in the Indian monsoon region, and how these changes may affect extreme rainfall events.
understanding the changing nature of rainfall variability in a warming climate and the associated risks in extreme rainfall events.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the low-frequency intraseaonal oscillatory modes of Indian summer Monsoon manifested by active phase, break phase, and extreme rainfall events are weakening over the past six decades.
the ISOs are weakening over the Indian region, which is compensated by a significant increase in the frequency of extreme rainfall events.
the monsoon low-frequency ISO modes over India have been weakening over the past six decades.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the relative strength and frequency of low-frequency intraseaonal variability has been significantly decreasing over India since 1958.
the monsoon low-frequency variability has weakened, and this has been compensated by the gain in the non-periodic variability.

the relative strength (i.e. the intensity) of low-frequency ISO modes has been decreasing over the past 60 years, and this is accompanied by a redistribution of rainfall intensity towards non-periodic extremes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the frequency and intensity of extreme rainfall events are not only associated with the strength of low-frequency modes of ISOs but also depend on the relative strength of synoptic-scale modes of ISO variability and the phase of monsoon ISO cycle.
the probability of extreme events is increasing, which is not only a function of mean monsoon rainfall, but also of its temporal distribution.
the relative contribution of low-frequency ISO modes to extreme rainfall is decreasing over India, while the contribution of extreme modes is increasing.
